# Context-borne lexical contagion — concept pack

## Vocabulary

- **self**: Context-borne lexical contagion (5/3)

## Definitions

- [statement] Scoping: prompt wording effects on task performance are not simply predicted by word frequency or perplexity, and prompts transfer poorly across datasets and models; a single modal-verb change moved performance up to 17 points in the tested older models (2023, LLaMA/OPT). Do not extrapolate fixed contagion rules from vocabulary frequency. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2311.01967 · keywords: Context-borne lexical contagion

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Repetition priming behaves differently in base LLMs, instruct LLMs and humans; instruction tuning appears to shift models toward more controlled processing, so contagion strength cannot be assumed identical across base and tuned models. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-31) — https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.14681 · keywords: Context-borne lexical contagion

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] LLMs reliably repeat contextual content faithfully rather than relying only on internal parameters; RepeatLeakage exploits this to extract system prompts from GPT-Store apps and ChatGPT contexts, and the copy-from-context ability cannot be disabled without hurting core capability. (medium confidence) — https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/34832 · keywords: Context-borne lexical contagion · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04484

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Anthropic's official prompting guide states that the formatting style used in a prompt may influence Claude's response style, and advises matching prompt style to desired output style; removing markdown from the prompt can reduce markdown in the output. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices · keywords: Context-borne lexical contagion · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04484
- [statement] In controlled dative-completion experiments, structurally primed completions show greater lexico-semantic repetition of context, i.e. structural, lexical and semantic alignment reinforce each other during generation (EMNLP 2026 Findings, submitted 2026-09-03). (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-03) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04484 · keywords: Context-borne lexical contagion
